title: Prompt Provenance Sketches
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notebook to capture ideas about tracking prompt provenance, curating few-shot exemplars, and rapid heuristics for identifying brittle cases. Intended for me-first experimentation — rough, iterative, and intended to seed later team docs if anything pans out.

High-level goals (what I want to get from this scratchpad):
- Maintain lightweight metadata for every exemplar: origin (copy/paste or synth), author, timestamp, prompt-template-id, context-window-dependency notes.
- Build a small curator flow to flag exemplars that cause hallucination, repetition, or style drift.
- Create a handful of resilient few-shot sets (3–7 shots) that generalize across instruction phrasing variants.
- Rapid failure triage checklist so I can annotate counterexamples quickly.

Why provenance matters (short):
- When a few-shot set degrades after a model/quant change, knowing where each exemplar came from helps decide rollback vs rewrite.
- Provenance -> easier A/B slice analysis: compare exemplars written by internal writers vs scraped examples.

Minimal JSON metadata I want per exemplar (NOT nested here — just a sketch of fields to capture in the DB):
- exemplar_id (uuid), source_label ("handwritten", "synthetic", "user-upload"), human_author, created_on, used_in_templates [list of template ids], failure_tags [list], token_len, short_summary (one line), test_prompt_ids [list], last_tested.

Prompt templates (working drafts) — keep terse and parameterized:
1) TEMPLATE: summarize-compact
- instruction: "Summarize the following text in 1–2 sentences, focusing on who, what, and why."
- context_slot: "<TEXT>"
- constraints: "No invented facts; if missing, say 'not provided'."
- few-shot-shotset: use 4 exemplars with varying domain tone (news, email, chat logs, research abstract).

2) TEMPLATE: plan-outline
- instruction: "Create a 3-step implementation plan to achieve the goal described. Include risks and a quick metric to track."
- context_slot: "<GOAL_DESC>"
- constraints: "Keep each step < 30 words."

3) TEMPLATE: persona-surface
- instruction: "Answer as a knowledgeable but concise product manager; 2–3 line responses."
- role_hint: "pm: pragmatic, clarifying questions encouraged"

Five-shot experiment (example exemplars for summarize-compact):
- Shot A (news): Input: short news paragraph about a city council vote. Output: 1-sentence summary, includes who and decision.
- Shot B (internal email): Input: email about delaying a feature. Output: 1-sentence summary with reason and next step.
- Shot C (chat log): Input: slack snippet; Output: 1-sentence summary capturing ask and owner.
- Shot D (abstract): Input: research abstract; Output: 1-sentence summary capturing main finding.
- Shot E (ambiguous): Input: a vague user report; Output: "not provided" if key facts missing.

Observed brittle behaviors (examples):
- Model hallucinates a stakeholder name when the exemplar mentions "the team" (seen on smaller models).
- Repetition: outputs duplicate the last shot's phrasing when sequence alignment is close (particularly after switching from 4-shot to 1-shot).
- Overfitting to stylistic cues: if exemplars are all passive-voice, the model defaults to passive voice even when active is clearer.

Quick triage checklist for a failing exemplar/shot:
1) Re-run with prompt-template explicit constraints appended (e.g., "Do not invent facts").
2) Run with example removed to test contribution.
3) Swap exemplar domain (news <-> email) to see cross-domain sensitivity.
4) Check tokenization boundary: is key info being split across tokens (potentially causing omission)?
5) Label failure type: hallucination | omission | style-drift | repetend | instruction-mismatch.

Mini case study: reproducible hallucination example
- Template: summarize-compact, 3-shot (A,B,C).
- Input: Slack message "Can we prioritize the billing bug?" (no stakeholder).
- Output observed: "Alice asked to prioritize the billing bug."
- Notes: exemplar B ends with an owner mention; model likely copied pattern and inserted a plausible name.
- Quick fix tried: replace exemplar B owner with placeholder "<OWNER>" then the model produced: "A team member requested prioritization." Better but less specific.

Testing matrix (lightweight):
- Dimensions: model size (small/med/large), quant (fp16/4bit), shots (0/1/3/5), exemplar-source (synthetic/handwritten), constraint-strictness (none/soft/strict).
- Metric slices: factual-accuracy, style-consistency (n-gram overlap to target style), repetition-rate, token-efficiency (avg tokens/output).

Short evaluation rubric (manual tagging to start):
- factual-accuracy: PASS | FAIL (if output contains invented proper nouns or incorrect facts).
- fidelity-to-instruction: GOOD | OK | POOR (did it follow length/format constraints?).
- usefulness: 1–5 (subjective).

Notes on exemplar curation heuristics (quick rules):
- Prefer exemplars with explicit labels ("Owner: X", "Decision: Defer") — explicit scaffolding reduces hallucination.
- Mix style: at least one exemplar in active voice, one with bullet list, one short sentence.
- Limit repeated phrasings across exemplars to avoid style overfitting.

Experiment ideas to run quickly (one-off runs):
- Synthesize neutral exemplars using a temperature=0.2 generation from the large model; compare to human-written exemplars for robustness. Tag which synthetic exemplars produce lower hallucination rates.
- Token-trimming: remove trailing punctuation in exemplars to see if it reduces repetend.
- Constraint priming: insert a short preface "Do not invent details" and measure delta.

Logging format for quick annotator notes (one line each):
- [2024-03-20] 3-shot summarizer: hallucinated org name -> label: hallucination; remediation: placeholder tokens in exemplar.
- [2024-03-22] 5-shot plan-outline: style-drift -> label: style-drift; remediation: add explicit "Active voice" constraint.

Open questions (to follow up):
- How to store exemplar fingerprints to detect near-duplicates without full-text hashing? (fast similarity vs exact match tradeoff)
- When should we prefer synthetic exemplars vs curated human ones for production templates?
- Is there a light-weight regression test we can run on deploy that focuses on the top 200 templates only?

Next actions (me):
- 1) Convert the winning 3 summarizer exemplars into JSON metadata fields and push to GHPR#1987 for visibility (by 2024-03-18).
- 2) Run quick A/B with and without "no-invent" preface across medium/large models (one day job).
- 3) Draft a tiny Confluence note: "Prompt provenance: minimal fields" and link.

Random micro-experiment log (raw outputs preserved):
- Prompt: summarize-compact + 3-shot (A,B,C) + slack message.
- Model output (med): "The billing team will prioritize the bug as requested by Sarah."
- Annotator note: name inserted (Sarah) not present — FAIL.

Personal heuristics (tacit knowledge):
- If a template has >2 hallucination incidents in 10 tests, demote it from active library until re-curated.
- Exemplars with too many domain-specific nouns need an anchor sentence that sets context ("This text is about billing.").

This doc is intentionally informal. I'll prune and formalize into a shared draft if we get signal from the small experiments. For now: capture concrete reproducible failure examples and a tiny metadata shape for provenance.

---
Scratch notes / TODOs (short):
- [ ] write a quick script to produce exemplar metadata CSV from current folder of test prompts.
- [ ] add a checksum field to exemplar metadata to detect accidental edits.
- [ ] add one synthetic exemplar per template and run sanity suite.
- [ ] file a short RFC if we want to add exemplar provenance to the Redwood prompt library schema.

End of scratchpad.
